course_name_original: Análisis Del Entorno Y Administración De Empresas (Plan 2024) (68044144)
course_name_en: Business Environment Analysis and Business Administration (2024 Plan) (68044144)

learning_outcomes.text: That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.

syllabus_topics: PART I: GENERAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT
The entrepreneur, the manager, the entrepreneur and the intrapreneur.
Concept, types and elements of structure
The expected value of perfect information
TOPIC 4. PROFIT, PROFITABILITY AND FINANCIAL EQUILIBRIUM
The cycles of company activity. Concepts of investment, cost, expense and payment
Costs in the company. Concept, types and structure
Basic financial documents. Balance sheet and income statement.
The company's economic-financial equilibrium and the working capital or operating fund
Concept and types of investments. Relevant elements
Concept and types of funding sources. Relevant elements
The required return on an investment
Valuation of investment and financing projects
Calculation of investment profitability and financing cost. Selection criteria
The weighted average cost of capital
Required return and the difference in risk between mutually exclusive investments
The usefulness of decision criteria and instruments in financial management. Investment programming and financial planning.
Economic risk and the break-even point.
The impact of sales variations on profit.
The impact of sales variations on profitability.
The relationship between financial profitability and operating profitability.
TOPIC 7. OBJECTIVES, ALTERNATIVES AND PRODUCTION DECISIONS
The added value of the production function.
The first decision: produce or buy
Production management: objectives and main types of strategic and tactical decisions
Main differences between manufacturing goods and providing services
Main types of production processes and technological alternatives
Principles in human factor management in production
Planning and control of productive activities
Types of inventory systems and models
The added value of the marketing function
The objective and the marketing mix
Short-term demand function and its elasticities
Market share forecasting and Markov chains
Marketing in the face of information and communication technologies (ICT)
Product identification. Brands, packaging and labels
The decision of price determination and its limitations
Measurement and control of advertising effectiveness
teaching_methods: Studying theoretical concepts and approaching practice with examples and specific cases (Resuelta Activities)
Using conceptual maps and initial questions for each chapter
Utilizing internet links for complementary activities
Completing objective self-assessment tests at the end of each chapter and globally
Practicing by solving exercises, problems, and cases from the practice book
Interaction with tutorial professors and other students
Posing questions to professors during student support hours
Participation in group activities organized by associate center tutors

assessment_methods.method: Mixed in-person exam (10 multiple-choice questions, 2 development questions)
Two voluntary evaluable activities (2 theoretical questions, 2 practical cases)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of two parts: 10 multiple-choice questions worth up to 5 points and two practical problems worth up to 5 points. There is no minimum score required in either part. The exam accounts for 100% of the base final grade, with a passing score of 5 points. The final grade can be increased by up to 10% based on the score from two voluntary evaluable activities, which must be submitted as a tutorial report before the end of the academic quarter.
